stdout_tail:
Both `result.json` and `analysis.py` are saved in the working directory.

**Finding:** A Gradient Boosting classifier trained to predict income (`>50K` vs `<=50K`) on the Adult dataset is well-calibrated overall — its predicted probabilities are within 0.96 percentage points of observed outcome frequencies on average (ECE, 10-bin, held-out test set), with AUC 0.926. The largest gap sits in the 0.7–0.9 predicted-probability range (up to ~3.8 points), reflecting mild overconfidence there, and isotonic post-hoc recalibration can tighten this further to 0.51 points without hurting discrimination. A Logistic Regression baseline is marginally better calibrated (ECE 0.83 pts) but has lower AUC (0.906).

parsed_result.summary: The Gradient Boosting classifier is well-calibrated overall: predicted probabilities differ from observed outcome frequencies by only 0.96 percentage points on average (ECE) on held-out data, below the 2-point materiality threshold, though it shows mild overconfidence in the 0.7-0.9 predicted-probability range (worst single-bin gap, MCE, of 3.76 points). It is very slightly less calibrated than a Logistic Regression baseline (ECE=0.83 pts), and isotonic post-hoc recalibration tightens its ECE further to 0.51 points without hurting discrimination (AUC 0.926 -> 0.926).
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Expected Calibration Error (10-bin, raw Gradient Boosting model)
parsed_result.direction: well-calibrated overall (ECE well under 2pp), with mild overconfidence in the 0.7-0.9 probability range
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Binary target = 1 if class=='>50K'. Missing categorical values (workclass, occupation, native-country) filled with 'Missing' category rather than dropped (~6% of rows affected). 75/25 stratified train/test split, random_state=42. Numeric features standardized; categorical features one-hot encoded. Primary model: GradientBoostingClassifier (n_estimators=200, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.1) chosen as a model class known to be prone to overconfidence, making calibration a non-trivial question; Logistic Regression fit as a naturally-calibrated baseline for comparison. Calibration measured via Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Maximum Calibration Error (MCE) using 10 equal-width probability bins on held-out test predictions, cross-checked against sklearn's quantile-binned calibration_curve; Brier score and ROC-AUC reported alongside. Post-hoc isotonic recalibration via 5-fold CalibratedClassifierCV (fit only on the training set) tests whether miscalibration is fixable. Miscalibration materiality threshold set subjectively at ECE > 0.02 (2 percentage points).
